newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia beheads Pakistani drug smuggler.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia beheads Pakistani drug smuggler.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Friday beheaded a Pakistani man convicted of drug smuggling.
The conservative kingdom has publicly executed at least 64 people so far this year compared with a total of 68 convicted criminals in 1996.

An interior ministry statement carried by the official Saudi Press Agency said the Pakistani man was beheaded by the sword on Friday in the capital Riyadh. A Saudi man was beheaded on Wednesday for murdering another Saudi national.
Saudi Arabia enforces Islamic sharia law by publicly beheading convicted murderers, rapists, drug smugglers and other criminals.
London-based Amnesty International and two Pakistani women's groups urged Saudi Arabia on Thursday to show leniency to several Pakistani children and women arrested for drug offences.
The human rights group asked Riyadh to immediately clarify the fate of seven Pakistani children arrested with eight women and four men -- all of whom may face the death penalty.
Amnesty said it was not known whether the 19 Pakistanis, arrested on January 19 at Jeddah airport for allegedly concealing heroin, had been tried or if they had been permitted legal counsel.
